description: Sector overlay for U.S. insurance institutions, producers, policyholder documentation, claims, market conduct, data security, AML where applicable, and policyholder-protection documentation.

metadata.scope: United States-only sector overlay controls for Insurance. Intended to be used with core_control_library.
metadata.source_note: Source basis revalidated against authoritative U.S. federal statutes, regulations, agency and regulator materials, and applicable model/professional or industry standards available through 2026-08-30. This rule pack remains an evidence-screening control set, not legal advice, and requires qualified legal/compliance review before production reliance. State, territorial, tribal, and local requirements may impose additional obligations.
metadata.external_knowledge_policy: No external knowledge is introduced during document evaluation. Regulatory source mappings live only in this versioned rule pack.

primary_sources.name: NAIC Insurance Data Security Model Law (#668) and state-adoption resources
NAIC Model Laws and state-action resources
FinCEN insurance company AML program resources
FTC/GLBA privacy and safeguards materials
used_for: nonpublic personal information safeguards where applicable

rules.title: State insurance licence, producer, or carrier authorization evidence is present
rules.summary: Checks for state insurance department, licence/license, certificate of authority, producer, broker, or carrier authorization evidence.

metadata.evidence_expectation: The reviewed document/document set should contain direct textual evidence for this control, or the engine should return missing/review_required according to the rule strategy.
metadata.review_guidance: A qualified U.S. legal/compliance reviewer must confirm applicability, jurisdictional scope, legal sufficiency, and whether absence of textual evidence should be treated as non-compliance.

rules.title: Insurance data-security program evidence is present
rules.summary: Checks for information-security-program, cybersecurity-event investigation, regulator notification, and third-party oversight evidence where the applicable state has enacted Model #668 or comparable insurance data-security requirements; Model #668 is not itself a uniform federal mandate.
